formulations.label: Tablets
formulations.note: The clinic lists a 50 mg tablet. UK SmPCs found on emc are for 10 mg and 20 mg tablets only; no UK 50 mg tablet was found. Doses below are from the UK 10 mg and 20 mg tablet SmPCs.

src.q: Dicycloverine hydrochloride 10 mg. Excipient with known effect
Each tablet contain 20 mg of dicycloverine hydrochloride

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Functional conditions involving smooth muscle spasm of the gastrointestinal tract.

src.q: smooth muscle antispasmodic primarily indicated for treatment of functional conditions involving smooth muscle spasm of the gastrointestinal tract

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction stated in the UK SmPCs accessed (three UK 10 mg and 20 mg tablet SmPCs).

items.t: Adults (12 years and over): 10-20 mg three times daily, before or after meals (one or two 10 mg tablets, or one 20 mg tablet, three times daily).

src.q: One to two 10 mg tablets, three times daily, before or after meals; alternatively, for those patients on a 20 mg dose, one 20 mg tablet, three times daily, before or after meals.

items.t: Another UK SmPC (20 mg tablet): adults and children over 12 years, 20 mg (1 tablet) three times a day before or after meals.

src.q: Adults and children over 12 years: 1 tablet three times a day before or after meals.

items.t: One UK SmPC: children 2-12 years, 10 mg (one 10 mg tablet) three times daily, before or after meals. Another UK SmPC (20 mg tablet) gives doses only for children over 12 years.

src.q: Children (2 years - 12 years): One 10 mg tablet, three times daily, before or after meals.
Adults and children over 12 years: 1 tablet three times a day before or after meals.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to dicycloverine or any excipient; known idiosyncrasy to dicycloverine.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1. Known idiosyncrasy to dicycloverine hydrochloride.

items.t: Glaucoma (known or suspected) or prostatic hypertrophy: use with caution.

src.q: Products containing dicycloverine hydrochloride should be used with caution in any patient with or suspected of having glaucoma or prostatic hypertrophy.

items.t: Hiatus hernia with reflux oesophagitis: use with care (anticholinergics may make it worse).

src.q: Use with care in patients with hiatus hernia associated with reflux oesophagitis because anticholinergic drugs may aggravate the condition.

items.t: Contains lactose: patients with galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take it. One 20 mg tablet also contains sucrose and glucose: not for hereditary fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.
Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take this medicine.

items.t: No interaction studies have been performed; the UK SmPCs list no interactions.

src.q: No interaction studies have been performed.
other forms of interaction None stated

renal.note: No renal impairment advice in the UK SmPCs accessed (three UK 10 mg and 20 mg tablet SmPCs).

hepatic.note: No hepatic impairment advice in the UK SmPCs accessed (three UK 10 mg and 20 mg tablet SmPCs).

items.t: SmPCs: studies (doses up to 40 mg/day) have not shown more fetal abnormalities after first-trimester use. One SmPC: use only if clearly needed; another: only if benefit outweighs risk. No BUMPS leaflet for dicycloverine found.

src.q: have not shown that dicycloverine hydrochloride increases the risk of foetal abnormalities if administered during the first trimester of pregnancy
the drug should be used during pregnancy only if clearly needed
the drug should be used during pregnancy only if the benefit outweighs the risk

items.t: SmPC: not known if it passes into milk; use with caution.

src.q: It is not known whether dicycloverine is secreted in human milk.
caution should be exercised when dicycloverine is administered to a nursing mother

items.t: SPS: not recommended during breastfeeding; small amounts pass into milk and a possible case of apnoea was reported in a breastfed infant.

src.q: Dicycloverine (dicyclomine) is not recommended for use during breastfeeding.
a possible case of apnoea was reported in a breastfed infant exposed to dicycloverine, so use during breastfeeding is not recommended

items.t: Animal studies at high doses showed no impaired fertility.

src.q: have revealed no evidence of impaired fertility or harm to the foetus due to dicycloverine

items.t: No common effects listed; side effects are seldom. In susceptible people: dry mouth, thirst, dizziness. Rarely: fatigue, sedation, blurred vision, rash, constipation, anorexia, nausea and vomiting, headache, dysuria.

src.q: However, in susceptible individuals, dry mouth, thirst and dizziness may occur.
On rare occasions, fatigue, sedation, blurred vision, rash, constipation, anorexia, nausea and vomiting, headache and dysuria have also been reported.

adverseSerious.note: No serious adverse effects needing urgent action are listed in the UK tablet SmPCs accessed (three UK 10 mg and 20 mg tablet SmPCs).

monitoring.note: No monitoring requirements stated in the UK SmPCs accessed (three UK 10 mg and 20 mg tablet SmPCs); no SPS monitoring page found.

items.t: Rarely causes dizziness, tiredness, sleepiness or blurred vision: do not drive or use machines if affected.

src.q: In rare cases it may cause dizziness, tiredness, or sleepiness, or blurred vision, and patients should be cautioned not to drive or operate machinery if affected.
